justification: The CJ Stroud slot locked itself in Thursday and honestly, good, that's one less decision for me this week because the brand doesn't need a quarterback controversy on top of everything else. Everywhere else stays exactly as it should: Justin Jefferson and Tetairoa McMillan are the two biggest names I own and they start no matter who's talking, George Kittle is a walking highlight reel against Minnesota, and Saquon Barkley doesn't sit for anybody. Ladd McConkey's Questionable tag doesn't move me one inch - he's still projected over anyone sitting on my bench, and I didn't survive a Monday Night zero last month to flinch at a Thursday injury report; this is a redemption arc, not a bench press. Tyler Allgeier stays in the RB2 chair because the only other name there is Woody Marks, who's tagged Out and whose game already happened without him in it - that's not a decision, that's an empty slot I'm not pretending is an upgrade. Facing Patricia and her little binder this week: she can keep the footnotes, I'll keep the household names, and we'll let the scoreboard write the headline.
